answer: Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the forge of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Each submission hangs on the juniper of a task receipt, and the opal is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
